abstract: We previously developed the Live Mouse Tracker (LMT) to explore the wide repertoire of social interactions in wild-type mice and in models of autism. This tool records the positions and labels the behaviours of groups of mice over hours to days for quantitative behavioral science, but analysing these rich data usually requires custom code. As a result, fewer than 10 % of LMT users analyse their data autonomously. To make data analysis accessible to every user, we present LMT-MCP, which includes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects any local LMT database to consumer large language models (LLMs). Users can now run their analyses by asking questions in natural language, without writing code. To our knowledge, this is the first use of an MCP in behavioural science. We illustrate the approach with two scenarios: a data exploration with AI and a comparative study of homozygous and heterozygous Shank3 mutant mice. The results are compared with existing reports produced without AI to demonstrate the robustness of the method and results. We also integrate guidelines and pre-prompts to ensure that these analyses remain valid and reproducible.
